correctness.rationale: Fixed-axis allowed rankings verified: four equiprobable ballots with peaks (1/4,1/2,1/4). For every odd n, Condorcet middle iff a,c<=r; other Condorcet winners are first-preference majorities, safe under IRV. The universal tie-insensitive failure event is exactly a,c<=r and b<min(a,c). The multinomial sum uses 2^b central ballot types. For the limit, offsets u,v>=1 produce a congruence-restricted absolutely summable lattice series; gamma log-convexity bounds each ratio by 1, fixed offsets converge to 1, and Stirling gives the stated normalization. Each residue sum is evaluated by elementary geometric series. Exact independent ballot and tie-breaking enumeration at n=1,3,5,7 matched the formula; n=9..31 exact computations further check finite values. Finite checks are not the proof of the asymptotic.

originality.rationale: The deterministic three-candidate center squeeze is explicitly covered by Correa-Lopera (2025), while the four-ballot uniform single-peaked culture is known from Walsh-related literature. After treating both as premises rather than discoveries, the added exact finite tie-independent failure probability and the 3-residue positive sharp large-electorate coefficients are not covered by the inspected full primary passages. Targeted actual alias/equivalence searches and mathematical comparison with related election findings did not identify a stronger result. Residual possibility of equivalent earlier results in broader voting-paradox compilations requires external literature review.
residual_risks: The comprehensive 2010 book by Gehrlein and Lepelley, Voting Paradoxes and Group Coherence: The Condorcet Efficiency of Voting Rules, could contain a related exact IRV probability but was not available in relevant full text; catalog/review evidence alone is not treated as disproving coverage.
The 1999 Vandercruyssen working paper on voting-procedure Condorcet efficiency was observed by abstract only; it reports simulations and its exact tables, if any, were not inspected.
Equivalent sharp coefficient results under large-deviation or three-candidate Hare terminology could remain undiscovered; search absence is not uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: Condorcet loss under ranked-choice is a substantive and widely studied election-design risk. The same deterministic center-squeeze event was known; the result supplies its exact finite frequency for independent uniform single-peaked ranked ballots, the exponential risk rate, and nontrivial three-phase lattice oscillation in the sharp prefactor, allowing comparison of rare-event risk across finite electorate sizes. This is not a generic restatement of the median voter theorem or an arbitrary count; it is a precise rule- and culture-specific reliability law. Interpretations are restricted to the explicit culture and all-tie-break event.
